narrative: A human-driven car first struck a pedestrian, sending her into the path of a Cruise robotaxi. The Cruise vehicle struck her and then moved toward the curb, dragging her roughly 20 feet. Federal investigators linked this SGO report ID to Cruise's software recall; California suspended its driverless permits after the incident.
attribution: NHTSA investigation and California DMV; media accounts of the same event

narrative: A Cruise driverless vehicle and a San Francisco fire engine responding to an emergency collided at an intersection. News coverage reported that a passenger in the robotaxi went to the hospital. Accounts differed on the vehicles' movements and right of way; the SGO entry lists a serious injury.
attribution: CBS San Francisco and ABC7 San Francisco; SGO report

narrative: Media accounts describe a seven-vehicle crash at Sixth and Harrison in which a speeding human-driven Tesla struck vehicles in traffic, including an unoccupied Waymo. One person in another vehicle died. The Waymo's involvement in the crash does not mean it caused the fatality; police investigated the Tesla driver's actions.
attribution: CBS San Francisco and San Francisco Chronicle reporting, matched to the Waymo SGO entry

narrative: Dallas police told local media that another SUV first struck a pedestrian and propelled him into the path of a driverless Waymo traveling the opposite direction. He died. The SGO reports a fatality involving the Waymo; the police account describes a sequence involving both vehicles and is not a final fault determination.
attribution: Dallas police as reported by CBS Texas and NBC 5 Dallas

narrative: Los Angeles reporting described a car that struck a pedestrian and then collided with a Waymo traveling in the opposite lane. The pedestrian was seriously injured. The SGO entry lists a serious injury in a crash involving a passenger car; the reporting does not establish the Waymo as the vehicle that struck the pedestrian.
attribution: Los Angeles Times reporting and Waymo's account as quoted in local coverage
